newsitem.title: USA: CVS picks Cordiant unit for ads.
newsitem.headline: CVS picks Cordiant unit for ads.

text.p: CVS Corp said on Tuesday it selected Cordiant Plc's Bates USA as its new advertising agency after an intensive search.
Industry sources said Bates, which beat out four other finalists for the CVS account, will oversee a television and radio broadcast campaign that will total about $65 million next year.
Bates will begin rolling out by the fourth quarter broadcast ads to build the CVS brandname. CVS completed its takeover of Revco for $2.9 billion in stock earlier this year.
"Revco was a very, very strong drug store chain, and did business in most geographic locations different than ours," Jack Kramer, senior vice president of advertising with CVS, told Reuters.
"We need to have a strong branding campaign, that enables the people in markets where we have not operated to know us and understand us," he said.

Before the merger, CVS was located primarily in the New England and mid-Atlantic states, while Revco was in the Southeast and Midwest. The merged company, which will use the CVS name, is the second-largest drug store chain in terms of revenues to Walgreen Co.

Ingalls, Quinn and Johnson of Boston had been CVS' ad agency with responsibility for both creative and electronic media buying. CVS recently selected TBS Media Management Inc of New York to manage its electronic media buying.
